quickAnswer: For seven days, choose Beijing plus Xi'an or Shanghai. With ten days, follow the classic Beijing-Xi'an-Shanghai route. With fourteen days, add Guilin for landscapes or Chengdu for food and pandas without turning the trip into a daily transfer marathon.

sections.title: Quick Picker
sections.summary: Choose two cities for seven days, three for ten, or add nature and regional stops with fourteen.

rows: A first look with minimal transfers
Adding nature, pandas, or regional food

sections.title: Route 1: The Golden Triangle
sections.summary: Combine Beijing, Xi'an and Shanghai, leaving time between the sightseeing blocks for travel.
items: Beijing: 3 days for the Forbidden City, Great Wall, hutongs, and imperial history.
Xi'an: 2 days for the Terracotta Warriors, city wall, and Muslim Quarter.
Shanghai: 3 days for the Bund, neighborhoods, museums, and modern city life.
Add a Suzhou day trip when your schedule has at least one flexible Shanghai day.

sections.title: Route 2: Culture Plus Nature
sections.summary: Combine Beijing and Xi'an with Guilin and Yangshuo for a landscape-focused finish.
items: Begin with Beijing and Xi'an for China’s essential historical arc.
Continue to Guilin and Yangshuo for the Li River, karst landscapes, and a slower finish.
Use this route when scenery matters more than finishing in Shanghai.

sections.title: Route 3: Pandas and Mountains
sections.summary: Combine Chengdu and Zhangjiajie with enough time for the transfer and mountain weather.
items: Base in Chengdu for pandas, Sichuan food, teahouses, and a relaxed urban pace.
Continue to Zhangjiajie for dramatic sandstone peaks and hiking viewpoints.
Allow a buffer day because the transfer is longer and mountain weather can affect plans.

sections.title: Train or Flight?
sections.summary: Compare the complete hotel-to-hotel journey rather than flight or train duration alone.
items: When a direct high-speed train fits your schedule and takes under about five hours, compare it with flying using total door-to-door time.
Check the actual train, stations and journey duration on Railway 12306. Include transfers, station or airport checks and the arrival time before deciding.
Fly when the rail journey is long, the flight schedule is substantially better, or you are connecting distant regions.
Avoid one-night city stops. Two or three nights per major destination makes a first trip more enjoyable.

faqs.question: Is seven days enough for a first trip to China?
faqs.answer: Yes, if you choose two cities. Beijing plus Xi'an emphasizes history; Beijing plus Shanghai gives a stronger old-and-new contrast.

faqs.question: What is the best 10-day China itinerary?
faqs.answer: The classic first-time route is Beijing for three days, Xi'an for two, and Shanghai for three, using the remaining time for transfers and a Suzhou day trip.

faqs.question: Should I add Guilin or Chengdu to a 14-day trip?
faqs.answer: Choose Guilin for landscapes and outdoor time. Choose Chengdu for pandas, Sichuan food, and a more relaxed city experience.

faqs.question: Should I book trains or flights between Chinese cities?
faqs.answer: Use high-speed rail when the journey is under about five hours. Compare total door-to-door time rather than the scheduled flight duration alone.
